 Academy Award winner and Hollywood icon Denzel Washington joins forces with Academy Award nominee and fellow Hollywood icon Mark Wahlberg in an action thriller in an oddly unsung action thriller that's streaming free after being cut from Netflix . Able to leap from violent run-ins with ruthless criminals to more comedic buddy-cop shenanigans, the action outing leans perfectly into what makes both actors so popular, with Washington bringing his effortless charm while Wahlberg offers his scrappy, blue-collar appeal.

 Washington & Wahlberg Wisecrack While Wreaking Revenge
 Directed by Baltasar Kormákur and starring Denzel Washington as DEA Special Agent Robert "Bobby Beans" Trench and Mark Wahlberg as U.S. Navy Special Operations Petty Officer 1st Class Michael "Stig" Stigman, the pair are locked and loaded like never before in 2 Guns . Based on the comic book series of the same name, the duo find themselves doing battle with an assortment of major names including Bill Paxton, James Marsden, Fred Ward, and Edward James Olmos as they fight to dodge gunfire from all sides. And that includes from each other. 
 You see, for the past year, DEA agent Bobby Trench (Washington) and U.S. Navy intelligence officer Marcus Stigman (Wahlberg) have been working undercover as members of a narcotics syndicate. But neither one knows the other is undercover. Instead, they assume the other is a crook, and when their attempt to infiltrate a Mexican drug cartel and recover millions goes awry, the men are disavowed by their superiors. With their secret out, they must join forces and go on the run lest they wind up in jail or a grave. 
 '2 Guns' Is Well Worth a Watch (Especially Now Its Free)

 2 Guns was met with mixed reviews at the time, landing scores of 64% from critics on Rotten Tomatoes, alongside 66% from audiences on the Popcornmeter. Looking back at the reviews, audiences were either enamored with the '80-style action throwback and banter between Wahlberg and Washington...or they found the whole experience uninspired and grating. 
 But 2 Guns has plenty to offer, with Washington and Wahlberg lighting up the screen with their bromantic back-and-forth before lighting up the screen even more with an array of shootouts and explosions. The perfect decompressing action effort that gets by on its charm and desire to entertain, 2 Guns has yet to spark the once-discussed sequel, 3 Guns , but the idea of Bobby Beans and Stig wisecracking together again while dodging danger is an exciting one. 2 Guns was recently cut from Netflix, but is now available to stream free (with ads) on YouTube .

 Some might argue that combining comedy with action can create a refreshing viewing experience, drawing audiences who appreciate both genres. Others might contend that this hybrid can often feel forced, leading to a disjointed film experience that lacks coherence. Additionally, some viewers might suggest that the success of such films greatly depends on the actors' ability to balance humor and action, which in the case of 2 Guns, seemed to resonate with fans, while critics were less impressed.
